## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

# OMG (Oh My GitHub) agent instructions

Do not implement, suggest, report, or propose security issues unless the user explicitly asks for a security review.
Inspect the OpenCode implementation at `/Users/igor/Documents/ChatGPT/opencode` and [anomalyco/opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) for related requests.

## Wiki index

- [OpenCode workflow](wiki/opencode.md)
- [Test OpenCode execution](wiki/opencode-v2-experiment.md)
- [Oh My Github App](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/oh-my-github-app.md)
- [Temporary Mac SSH access](wiki/access.md)
- [Testing and verification](wiki/testing.md)
- [OmGithub publishing](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/omgithub.md)


## Main project file

The main project file is [.github/workflows/opencode.yml](.github/workflows/opencode.yml).

Keep the local [game issue E2E skill](.agents/skills/game-issue-e2e/SKILL.md)
aligned with this workflow. Create an issue with `OpenCode` and only user-requested mode labels already attached, to start the native `issues.opened` listener. Wait only for the
initial OpenCode session link during E2E kickoff. Install the listener on the
default branch before requesting execution. Validate author access and freeze
the request inside Actions before starting the reusable execution job.
Set repository variable `OPENCODE_ACCESS=everyone` to accept any issue author
for labeled issues. Keep the App as a setup
helper. Use Actions concurrency to serialize each issue.
Store `branch` in an `omgithub-request:v1` JSON HTML comment to select the
project checkout, result base, and workflow. Let default-branch preparation
dispatch the selected branch. Run preparation and OpenCode in that branch run.

## Shell timing

When writing shell scripts,
always add explicit per-command execution-time measurements between commands.
Use `/usr/bin/time -p` or a small timing helper around each meaningful command;
the outer command duration is not sufficient because it hides which step is
slow or hung. Use `/usr/bin/time` only in scripts; do not invoke it directly in
interactive shell commands.

## Ideas

Store durable implementation ideas as individual Markdown files under
`./ideas/`, using descriptive kebab-case filenames such as
`ideas/opencode-oauth-env-auth.md`.




## Links in handoffs

When a relevant URL or stable identifier exists, include a clickable Markdown
link in the user-facing response. Link GitHub issues, Actions runs, pull
requests, commits, releases, public app URLs, and Codex tasks/threads rather
than reporting only their numbers or plain text. For Codex tasks/threads, use
the `codex://threads/<thread-id>` URL format.

When mentioning a commit, append its relative age in hours or days.

## OpenCode GitHub Actions

To execute an issue, create it with `OpenCode` and only mode labels explicitly requested by the user.
Check for a native `issues` run and successful preparation.
The workflow starts a temporary AgentsWeb SSH session,
verifies it, runs OpenCode, and cleans up the SSH session afterward.

When monitoring a triggered run, use `gh run watch <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --exit-status` for overall job status.
Do not use `gh run view --log` to read logs from a running task: GitHub reports that
logs are unavailable until completion. Use `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>`
for the live Actions log over SSH. Do not use tight `for` loops around `gh run list`,
which needlessly consume GitHub API rate limit.

Free OpenCode models are limited per egress IP, not per account.
Treat a local `FreeUsageLimitError` 429 as local only.
Read the runner's own `Selected model` and provider errors before blaming quota.
Use `retryAfterMs` as the reset bound.
Run repeated V2 tests with a connected provider; do not spend the free allowance on retries.

Interrupting a V2 turn before the assistant message projects leaves no stopped message to save.
Wait for that assistant message before requiring the interrupted idle marker.

To connect to an issue's live worker, find its run ID with
`gh run list --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --workflow opencode.yml --status in_progress`,
then run `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>` to discover the host and port and SSH
with `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb` as shown by the helper.

When the user asks to check a live OpenCode workflow, always pull the runner logs
over SSH first, using `scripts/ssh-run-log.sh` or a targeted SSH read from the
same runner. Base the answer on those logs before discussing whether an action
is confirmed; do not lead with a generic inability-to-confirm statement when
live log evidence can be collected.

For real-time inspection from a live temporary SSH session, use the helper:

```sh
bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>
```

The helper discovers the temporary SSH command from the triggering issue or pull
request, then follows the freshest `_diag/pages` log. The runner uploads chunks from
`_diag/blocks` to GitHub. Do not print environment files, tokens, or private keys while
inspecting the runner.

## Mac SSH access

The Mac private key stays at `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`. Its public key is
stored in the repository Actions secret `AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY`. The issue
commented by the workflow contains a directly usable command such as:

```sh
ssh -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
```

The command works only while the corresponding Actions job is running.

## Connecting to a live OpenCode worker

Use the repository helper to discover the worker host and port from the broker
or issue comment. It uses the persistent local key `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`:

```sh
bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub
```

For an interactive shell, reuse the host and port printed by the helper and
use the same key:

```sh
ssh -tt -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no \
  -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null \
  -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb \
  -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
```

Do not substitute the generated runner key under `sshworker/outputs/keys/`; it
can produce a misleading `Permission denied (publickey)` result. Temporary
worker SSH access ends when the Actions job and session are cleaned up. Never
print secrets while inspecting a worker.

export const SAVE_KEY = 'honeymoon-hive-save-v1'

export const REBIRTH_REQUIREMENT = 25000
export const REBIRTH_BONUS = 0.2

const SUFFIXES = ['', 'K', 'M', 'B', 'T', 'Qa', 'Qi', 'Sx', 'Sp', 'Oc', 'No', 'Dc']

export function fmt(value, forceDecimals = 0) {
  if (!Number.isFinite(value)) return '0'
  if (value < 0) return '0'
  if (value < 1000) {
    if (forceDecimals > 0 || (value < 10 && value % 1 !== 0)) {
      return value.toFixed(value < 10 ? Math.max(forceDecimals, 1) : forceDecimals)
    }
    return Math.round(value).toString()
  }
  let tier = 0
  let n = value
  while (n >= 1000 && tier < SUFFIXES.length - 1) {
    n /= 1000
    tier++
  }
  const decimals = n < 10 ? 2 : n < 100 ? 1 : 0
  return `${n.toFixed(decimals).replace(/\.0+$/, '').replace(/(\.\d)0$/, '$1')}${SUFFIXES[tier]}`
}

export function fmtRate(value) {
  if (value < 10) return value.toFixed(1).replace(/\.0$/, '')
  return fmt(value)
}

export function fmtTime(seconds) {
  if (!Number.isFinite(seconds) || seconds < 0) return '—'
  if (seconds < 60) return `${Math.ceil(seconds)}s`
  if (seconds < 3600) return `${Math.floor(seconds / 60)}m ${Math.floor(seconds % 60)}s`
  return `${Math.floor(seconds / 3600)}h ${Math.floor((seconds % 3600) / 60)}m`
}

  },

export const UPGRADE_BY_ID = Object.fromEntries(UPGRADES.map((u) => [u.id, u]))
export const TREE_WIDTH = 940
export const TREE_HEIGHT = 545

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// State + derived stats
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

export function createInitialState() {
  const unlocked = { meadow: true }
  const bees = {}
  BEE_TYPES.forEach((b) => (bees[b.id] = 0))
  bees.worker = 1
  return {
    version: SAVE_VERSION,
    honey: 0,
    jar: 0,
    lifetime: 0,
    runLifetime: 0,
    totalJars: 0,
    bees,
    upgrades: {},
    zone: 'meadow',
    unlocked,
    jelly: 0,
    rebirths: 0,
    sound: true,
    savedAt: Date.now(),
    createdAt: Date.now(),
    hintsSeen: {},
  }
}

export function derive(state) {
  const zone = ZONE_BY_ID[state.zone] || ZONES[0]
  let beeRate = 0
  let beeCount = 0
  for (const type of BEE_TYPES) {
    const count = state.bees[type.id] || 0
    beeRate += count * type.rate
    beeCount += count
  }

  let prodMul = 1
  let capMul = 1
  let valueMul = 1
  let autoEff = 0

  for (const up of UPGRADES) {
    const level = state.upgrades[up.id] || 0
    if (!level) continue
    if (up.prod) prodMul *= 1 + up.prod * level
    if (up.cap) capMul *= 1 + up.cap * level
    if (up.value) valueMul *= 1 + up.value * level
    if (up.auto) autoEff = Math.max(autoEff, up.auto)
  }

  const rebirthMul = 1 + state.jelly * REBIRTH_BONUS
  const rate = beeRate * prodMul * zone.prod * rebirthMul
  const capacity = 60 * capMul * zone.cap
  const value = valueMul * zone.value
  const fullBonus = 1.25
  const perSecondValue = rate * value

  return {
    zone,
    beeRate,
    beeCount,
    prodMul,
    capMul,
    valueMul,
    prodFromUpgrades: prodMul * zone.prod * rebirthMul,
    rebirthMul,
    autoEff,
    rate,
    capacity: Math.max(10, capacity),
    value,
    fullBonus,
    perSecondValue,
    fillTime: rate > 0 ? capacity / rate : Infinity,
    collectValue: state.jar * value * (state.jar >= capacity - 0.0001 ? fullBonus : 1),
  }
}

export function upgradeCost(up, level) {
  return Math.ceil(up.cost * Math.pow(up.growth, level))
}

export function isUpgradeUnlocked(state, up) {
  return up.req.every((id) => (state.upgrades[id] || 0) > 0)
}

export function beeCost(type, count) {
  return Math.ceil(type.cost * Math.pow(type.growth, count))
}

export function totalBeeCount(state) {
  return BEE_TYPES.reduce((sum, type) => sum + (state.bees[type.id] || 0), 0)
}

export function rebirthGain(state) {
  return Math.floor(Math.sqrt(Math.max(0, state.runLifetime) / REBIRTH_REQUIREMENT))
}

export function nextRebirthAt(state) {
  const next = rebirthGain(state) + 1
  return next * next * REBIRTH_REQUIREMENT
}

export function rebirthMultiplier(state) {
  return 1 + state.jelly * REBIRTH_BONUS
}

export function zoneUnlocked(state, zone) {
  return !!state.unlocked[zone.id]
}

export function bestBeeAvailable(state) {
  return BEE_TYPES.filter((b) => zoneUnlocked(state, ZONE_BY_ID[b.zone])).at(-1)
}

export function saveState(state) {
  try {
    state.savedAt = Date.now()
    localStorage.setItem(SAVE_KEY, JSON.stringify(state))
    return true
  } catch (err) {
    console.warn('Could not save game', err)
    return false
  }
}

export function loadState() {
  const fresh = createInitialState()
  try {
    const raw = localStorage.getItem(SAVE_KEY)
    if (!raw) return { state: fresh, loaded: false, elapsed: 0 }
    const parsed = JSON.parse(raw)
    if (!parsed || typeof parsed !== 'object') return { state: fresh, loaded: false, elapsed: 0 }
    const state = {
      ...fresh,
      ...parsed,
      bees: { ...fresh.bees, ...(parsed.bees || {}) },
      upgrades: { ...(parsed.upgrades || {}) },
      unlocked: { ...fresh.unlocked, ...(parsed.unlocked || {}) },
      hintsSeen: { ...(parsed.hintsSeen || {}) },
    }
    // Sanitise.
    if (!ZONE_BY_ID[state.zone]) state.zone = 'meadow'
    state.honey = Math.max(0, Number(state.honey) || 0)
    state.jar = Math.max(0, Number(state.jar) || 0)
    state.lifetime = Math.max(0, Number(state.lifetime) || 0)
    state.runLifetime = Math.max(0, Number(state.runLifetime) || 0)
    state.jelly = Math.max(0, Number(state.jelly) || 0)
    state.rebirths = Math.max(0, Number(state.rebirths) || 0)
    state.unlocked.meadow = true
    for (const id of Object.keys(state.unlocked)) if (!ZONE_BY_ID[id]) delete state.unlocked[id]
    for (const key of Object.keys(state.bees)) {
      if (!BEE_BY_ID[key]) delete state.bees[key]
      else state.bees[key] = Math.max(0, Math.floor(Number(state.bees[key]) || 0))
    }
    for (const key of Object.keys(state.upgrades)) {
      const up = UPGRADE_BY_ID[key]
      if (!up) delete state.upgrades[key]
      else state.upgrades[key] = Math.min(up.max, Math.max(0, Math.floor(Number(state.upgrades[key]) || 0)))
    }
    const elapsed = Math.max(0, (Date.now() - (Number(state.savedAt) || Date.now())) / 1000)
    return { state, loaded: true, elapsed }
  } catch (err) {
    console.warn('Could not load save', err)
    return { state: fresh, loaded: false, elapsed: 0 }
  }
}

export function resetState(state) {
  const fresh = createInitialState()
  fresh.sound = state.sound
  fresh.createdAt = state.createdAt
  fresh.hintsSeen = { ...state.hintsSeen }
  fresh.unlocked = { ...state.unlocked }
  fresh.zone = state.zone
  fresh.jelly = 0
  fresh.rebirths = 0
  return fresh
}

export function clearSave() {
  try {
    localStorage.removeItem(SAVE_KEY)
  } catch {}
}

  ctx.closePath()
}

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D Roblox-style honey simulator/incremental for phone/tablet: bees make honey, honey drips into a jar with animation, upgrades in a tree, better bees, rebirths, and unlockable themed zones with distinct bees/jars.

## Requirements
- 3D game, phone/tablet-first responsive layout with usable touch controls.
- Honey production from bees plus animated honey drizzle into a jar.
- Honey spent on upgrades structured as an upgrade tree (more honey, faster jar filling/value, auto-collect).
- Better bees and rebirth system.
- Unlock different zones with thematic bees and jars (e.g., desert island).
- No clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Vite + Three.js (three@0.187.0) static build, procedural 3D assets only (no external models).
- Two currencies conceptually: jar honey (auto-filled, stored for wallet honey) and wallet honey (spent). Full jar collection gives +25% bonus.
- Upgrade tree uses DOM/SVG overlay with 14 upgrade nodes, prerequisites, levels, and horizontal scroll on mobile.
- Five zones: Clover Meadow, Sunscorch Isle, Prism Hollow, Frostpetal Peaks, Gilded Sanctum, each with production/value/jar-capacity multipliers, unique jar tint/charm/label, native bee color, and procedural scenery.
- Six bee tiers: Worker, Bumble, Dune, Gem, Frost, Gilded Queen; higher tiers gated by zone unlocks.
- Rebirth gives royal jelly based on `floor(sqrt(runLifetime / 25000))`, each jelly +20% permanent flow; zones stay unlocked.
- Auto-collect upgrades (`Honey Tap` 50%, `Auto Pour` 100%) use hidden overflow accumulation to avoid lost production.
- Saved to `localStorage` with 5s autosave, visibility/pagehide saves, and offline catch-up capped at 8 hours.
- Exposed `window.__honeyGame` debug API for testing/screenshots.

## Work State
### Completed
- Installed Three.js and Vite; downloaded local Fredoka/Nunito woff2 fonts with OFL licenses.
- Created `index.html`, full mobile-first CSS, icon set, game data/economy, audio synth, save/load/offline logic.
- Created 3D world: floating island, beehive, wooden honey pipe, giant jar, animated vertex-wobbling honey stream, droplets/splash/bead, bees with wing flap and flight AI, themed zone scenery, particles, bursts, collect animation, full-jar sprite, camera orbit/tap.
- Created UI: HUD, jar meter, store button ring, toasts, floating gains, shop bottom sheet with tabs for upgrade tree, bees, zones, rebirth, help, confirmations, zone/rebirth flash overlays.
- Wired game loop, purchases, zone travel/unlock, rebirth, collect, sound toggle, hints, milestones, debug API.

### Active
- Not yet run/built or screenshot-tested; likely syntax/runtime bugs remain.

### Blocked
- None.

## Next Move
1. Fix obvious bug in `src/main.js` `rebirth()`: replace invalid `world.spawnUpgradeBurst(new (window.__THREE?.Vector3 || Object)())` with `world.spawnUpgradeBurst()`.
2. Run `npm run build` / start dev server on port 3002 and fix compile/runtime errors.
3. Use Playwright (`playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002`, resize mobile/tablet/desktop) to screenshot; verify jar drip animation, bees, jar fill, collect, upgrade tree, bee/zone/rebirth tabs, touch layout.
4. Tune 3D camera composition, lighting, jar/stream alignment, performance, z-indexes, and all UI text fit.
5. Test save/load/offline, zone unlock/travel, rebirth, auto-collect, and reset-save.
6. Verify no console errors; finalize README/assumptions and commit if required.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js`: game loop, economy actions, save/offline, debug API; contains known invalid rebirth burst line.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game/world.js`: main Three.js world, camera, hive, pipe, signs, zone switching, bees sync, resize.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game/jar.js`: jar glass/honey/ripples/label/themed charms/full sprite.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game/world-fx.js`: honey stream, splash, bursts, smoke, sparkles.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game/world-env.js`: five themed zone environments, particles, flower positions.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game/world-bees.js`: bee models, flight AI, visible bee spec builder.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game/data.js`: zones, bee types, upgrade tree, costs, derived stats, save/load.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/ui.js`: HUD/shop/tree/bees/zones/rebirth/help rendering and interactions.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/style.css`: all responsive/safe-area mobile styling.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/icons.js`: inline SVG icons and bee portraits.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: HUD, dock, modal, overlays markup.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game/audio.js`: procedural WebAudio SFX.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/start.sh`: uses runtime `default-start.mjs`; static/Vite project.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/package.json`: Vite/Three dependency scripts.

## Important Context
- Runtime supports Vite projects and builds automatically; `start.sh` runs the runtime default starter, screenshot capture via `capture.sh` or `playwright-cli`.
- Current git state: repository had only initial OpenCode workflow/README and setup scripts; all game files are newly created and uncommitted. `node_modules` ignored.
- `src/game/data.js` zones require `cap` multipliers (already added: meadow 1, desert 1.15, crystal 1.25, frost 1.35, gold 1.5).
- `world.js` uses `scene.environmentIntensity` and `RoomEnvironment`; if unsupported, it catches gracefully.
- In `rebirth()`, the invalid `world.spawnUpgradeBurst(...)` call will likely throw and must be fixed before testing.
- `world-bees.js` currently builds up to 18 owned bees plus 3 native decorative bees (21 total); consider lowering for mobile performance.
- `capture.sh`/runtime instructions: use headed Chromium/SwiftShader, serve at port 3002; save JPEG screenshots ≤1280px wide.
- The UI's `store` flow is functional, but no build/test has yet confirmed imports, CSS, or Three.js WebGL initialization.

export const REBIRTH_BONUS = 0.2

const SUFFIXES = ['', 'K', 'M', 'B', 'T', 'Qa', 'Qi', 'Sx', 'Sp', 'Oc', 'No', 'Dc']

export function fmt(value, forceDecimals = 0) {
  if (!Number.isFinite(value)) return '0'
  if (value < 0) return '0'
  if (value < 1000) {
    if (forceDecimals > 0 || (value < 10 && value % 1 !== 0)) {
      return value.toFixed(value < 10 ? Math.max(forceDecimals, 1) : forceDecimals)
    }
    return Math.round(value).toString()
  }
  let tier = 0
  let n = value
  while (n >= 1000 && tier < SUFFIXES.length - 1) {
    n /= 1000
    tier++
  }
  const decimals = n < 10 ? 2 : n < 100 ? 1 : 0
  return `${n.toFixed(decimals).replace(/\.0+$/, '').replace(/(\.\d)0$/, '$1')}${SUFFIXES[tier]}`
}

export function fmtRate(value) {
  if (value < 10) return value.toFixed(1).replace(/\.0$/, '')
  return fmt(value)
}

export function fmtTime(seconds) {
  if (!Number.isFinite(seconds) || seconds < 0) return '—'
  if (seconds < 60) return `${Math.ceil(seconds)}s`
  if (seconds < 3600) return `${Math.floor(seconds / 60)}m ${Math.floor(seconds % 60)}s`
  return `${Math.floor(seconds / 3600)}h ${Math.floor((seconds % 3600) / 60)}m`
}

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D Roblox-style honey simulator/incremental for phone/tablet: bees make honey, honey drips into a jar with animation, upgrades in a tree, better bees, rebirths, and unlockable themed zones with distinct bees/jars.

## Requirements
- 3D game, phone/tablet-first responsive layout with usable touch controls.
- Honey production from bees plus animated honey drizzle into a jar.
- Honey spent on upgrades structured as an upgrade tree (more honey, faster jar filling/value, auto-collect).
- Better bees and rebirth system.
- Unlock different zones with thematic bees and jars (e.g., desert island).
- No clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Vite + Three.js (`three@0.187.0`) static build; all art procedural, no external models.
- Wallet honey is spent; jar honey auto-fills and is collected manually/auto, with +25% full-jar bonus.
- Upgrade tree is a scrollable DOM/SVG overlay with 14 nodes, prerequisites, levels, and mobile drag hint.
- Five zones: Clover Meadow, Sunscorch Isle, Prism Hollow, Frostpetal Peaks, Gilded Sanctum; each has production/value/cap multipliers, unique jar tint/charm/label, native bee color, and scenery.
- Six bee tiers; higher tiers gated by zone unlocks. Visual swarm caps at 12 owned bee models plus 3 native decorative bees.
- Rebirth grants royal jelly via `floor(sqrt(runLifetime / 25000))`; each jelly gives +20% permanent flow. Zones remain unlocked; upgrades/swarm/honey reset.
- `Honey Tap` auto-collects full jars at 50% value; `Auto Pour` at 100%. Hidden overflow preserves production while auto-collecting.
- LocalStorage save with 5s autosave, visibility/pagehide saves, and 8-hour offline catch-up.
- `window.__honeyGame` debug API exposed for state, actions, travel, fill, reset, etc.
- Clouds drift in a bounded sine path so they remain in frame instead of drifting offscreen.
- Removed the 3D zone sign and decorative honey dipper, and removed the hive sign, to reduce clutter/occlusion and draw calls.
- Added `[hidden] { display:none !important }` because CSS display rules overrode the attribute.
- Erase-save now sets `saveDisabled` so pagehide/beforeunload do not immediately restore the cleared save.

## Work State
### Completed
- All game files created: Vite entry, mobile-first CSS, procedural 3D world, jar, honey stream/droplets, bees, five zone environments, upgrade tree, bees/zones/rebirth/help UI, audio, save/offline logic.
- Fixed known invalid rebirth burst call (`world.spawnUpgradeBurst()`).
- Added npm scripts `dev`, `build`, `preview`; `npm run build` passes.
- Fixed missing `addFence` reference in `world-env.js` (now uses `makeFence`).
- Fixed sky rendering black by replacing `Color.setHex(zone.sky[i])` with `setStyle(...)`; sky gradient now displays.
- Fixed shadow warning by switching `PCFSoftShadowMap` → `PCFShadowMap`.
- Removed undefined-material warnings in `world-env.js` `std()` via conditional spreads.
